P.text: A normal supported BLP lifecycle: supply via MonetrixVault.supplyToBlp(), which automatically registers a Vault-side 0x811 supplied slot in MonetrixAccountant.vaultSupplied, then withdraw max/full unwind via MonetrixVault.withdrawFromBlp().
P.evidence_quote: Uses a normal supported BLP lifecycle: supply, then withdraw max/full unwind

I.text: When a BLP position is fully unwound, the registry entry for the 0x811 supplied slot should be retired/removed so that MonetrixAccountant.totalBackingSigned() does not iterate a dead slot and perform a strict PrecompileReader.suppliedBalance() read that reverts if the external 0x811 slot is absent or unreadable.
I.evidence_quote: but `MonetrixVault.withdrawFromBlp()` never removes that registry entry when the BLP position is fully unwound.

V.text: After a normal BLP supply-then-full-withdraw lifecycle, the protocol can enter a state where totalBackingSigned(), surplus(), distributableSurplus(), and settle() all revert until a separate manual removeSuppliedEntry() cleanup is performed, causing protocol-wide accounting and settlement liveness failure (a DoS, not a theft bug).
V.evidence_quote: after a normal BLP supply-then-full-withdraw lifecycle, the protocol can enter a state where `totalBackingSigned()`, `surplus()`, `distributableSurplus()`, and `settle()` all revert until a separate manual `removeSuppliedEntry()` cleanup is performed.
